clue.text: Our claim about America is extraordinary

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the first two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their assertion concerning the USA is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it puts something round America, but here it is the anagram signal for 'Our claim' only.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something astonishing, beyond the normal course of nature: a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 21
Others rave about one's self-control

parts.note: the rest means the others, the remainder

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to rant is to rave, speak wildly
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is read as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A comment that other people rant about someone's admirable self-discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is holding oneself back, the exercise of self-discipline: a synonym.

clue.text: Split from leader of Champagne socialists

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Champagne

parts.note: the left is the political wing of socialists

explanation.surface: A rift within the so-called champagne socialists, wealthy left-wingers, caused by their leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champagne socialists' are well-off people with left-wing views, a British jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft is a past participle meaning divided or cut in two, as split is.

clue.text: Gyrating part of body in fat dancer's costume

indicators.note: in places the turned body part within the fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: gyrating means turning round, so the body part's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a toe is a part of the body

explanation.surface: An overweight performer spinning part of their body inside a stage outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gyrating' seems to describe the dancer's moves but is the reversal signal; 'fat' is a noun, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is the close-fitting one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Mysterious aircraft maintains bearing over lake, detective reveals

indicators.note: maintains means holds, so the aircraft holds the bearing inside it

parts.note: a UFO is an unidentified flying object
N, north, is a compass bearing
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
DS is Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A detective unveils a UFO keeping its course over a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfold a story is to disclose or lay it open bit by bit, so it reveals.

clue.text: Goad retreating rugby players heartlessly

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, a form of rugby

indicators.note: heartlessly removes all the inner part of players, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: An instruction to urge on a rugby team falling back without spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' strips all the inner letters of 'players', not just one; 'retreating' then turns the whole piece round.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is an incentive, or as a verb to urge on; goad is a synonym in both senses.

clue.text: Musician from Portugal appearing in seaside venue

indicators.note: appearing in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a pier is a seaside structure often holding a theatre or arcade
P is the international vehicle registration letter for Portugal

explanation.surface: A Portuguese musician performs at a seaside entertainment spot.
explanation.walkthrough: British seaside piers often had theatres for summer shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper is someone who plays the pipes or bagpipes, a kind of musician.

clue.text: Doctors, engineers and soldiers run into sailors

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
GIs are American soldiers

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the run abbreviation enters the sailors

parts.note: tars are sailors
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A list of military personnel and medics, with one running among the navy men.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a senior doctor below consultant grade, so doctors in that rank.

clue.text: Comparatively stinking rich see poor engulfing earth

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing, so the shuffled letters surround the earth abbreviation
poor means badly made, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: Seemingly about the stinking rich and the poor, with earth swallowed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stinking rich' is a false phrase: 'stinking' belongs to the definition, 'rich' to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheesier smell is more like ripe cheese, so more stinking in comparison.

clue.text: Is girl put out?

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Asking whether a young woman is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as annoyed; here it means published.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a stamp or a statement is to put it out, release it to the public.

clue.text: Article by bad penny, say, intended for mass market

parts.note: food gone off is bad
the is the definite article
e.g. (for example) is what say means here

explanation.surface: An item next to a counterfeit penny, perhaps, aimed at ordinary buyers.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes bought off the peg are ready-made in standard sizes rather than tailored, for the general market.

clue.text: Planned trip with publicity ace some time before autumn

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity
A is ace on playing cards
T is the abbreviation for time
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: An organised journey with a PR star, some time ahead of the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planned trip' sounds like a holiday; it is a deliberate stumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A pratfall is a staged comic fall, so a trip done on purpose.

clue.text: Touring centre of Chelsea, Cockney picks up posh types

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the hearing word goes around the central letter

parts.note: picks up means hears; a Cockney drops the H, giving 'ears

indicators.note: the centre of Chelsea is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A Londoner on a tour of Chelsea overhears upper-class people.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, are known for dropping their initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls are members of the nobility, so aristocratic, posh people.

clue.text: Villain beat up a knight, gatecrashing banquet

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash

indicators.note: gatecrashing means entering uninvited, so the pieces go inside the banquet

parts.note: a feast is a banquet
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A villain assaults a knight who barged into a feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat up' looks like an anagram or assault; it is LAM read upwards, MAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A malfeasant is a wrongdoer, someone guilty of misconduct, so a villain.

clue.text: A rum needs to capture island flavour

indicators.note: capture means hold inside, so the shuffled letters hold the island abbreviation
rum means strange, so the letters of needs are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rum drink needs an island taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed is the seed of anise, used to give a liquorice-like taste, so a flavour.

clue.text: Representative from record company's claim about Queen

parts.note: EMI is a British record company; with the 's it gives EMIS

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the claim word goes round the Queen

parts.note: to say is to claim
R is Regina, Queen

explanation.surface: A spokesperson for a record label makes an assertion concerning the band Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an envoy sent on a mission, a representative of someone.

clue.text: Start to study more sinuous snake

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of study

parts.note: lither means more supple and lithe, more sinuous

explanation.surface: Advice to begin examining a more twisting serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snake' is a verb here, not the reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: To snake is to move in a winding, gliding way, as one slithers.

clue.text: Fools outlaw whiskey in Kansas

parts.note: a hood is a gangster, an outlaw; also Robin Hood
whiskey is W in the NATO alphabet
KS is the postal abbreviation for Kansas

explanation.surface: A desperado knocking back whiskey in Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink is to deceive or trick, so to fool someone; both are verbs here.

clue.text: It appears in newspaper popular with German right

indicators.note: appears in puts it inside the newspaper

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times newspaper
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: Something printed in a paper popular with the German right wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting means suitable or proper, as right does in 'the right thing'.

clue.text: Light from space enveloping second city on mountain

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping round, so the space surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a gap is a space
LA is Los Angeles
M is an abbreviation for mountain listed in Collins

explanation.surface: A glow seen from space covering a second city on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: M for mountain is rare; Collins lists it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas lamp is a lamp burning gas, a source of light on old streets.

clue.text: Spooner's composer gave money to servant

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: Gustav Mahler was an Austrian composer
paid means gave money to

explanation.surface: A composer pays wages to his domestic help.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of MAHLER PAID gives PARLOUR MAID; the swap works by sound, not spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A parlourmaid was a household servant who waited at table and tended the sitting room.

clue.text: It symbolises rebirth of hope in troubled times

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of hope and in are mixed up

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: A statement that something stands for renewed hope during hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: The phoenix is the mythical bird that burns and rises from its ashes, an emblem of renewal.

clue.text: Range of canned peas oddly reduced

indicators.note: oddly reduced means the odd letters are cut, keeping the even ones of canned peas

explanation.surface: A selection of tinned peas sold at a strange discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a product line; it is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain chain of South America, a range.

clue.text: Coin another term for school with no restrictions

indicators.note: with no restrictions means the limits, the outer letters, are removed

parts.note: to educate is to school someone

explanation.surface: Seems to ask for a different word for school, free of rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe in earlier centuries.

clue.text: Doctor who's on deck for decisive engagement

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of who's are rearranged

parts.note: on the deck means floored, knocked down

explanation.surface: Doctor Who aboard ship, about to fight a final battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' reads as the TV show, but 'Doctor' is the anagram signal on WHO'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is a final confrontation that settles a dispute, a deciding clash.

clue.text: Curious journalist raised objection

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: rum means curious, odd
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: An inquisitive reporter voiced a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised objection' reads as a phrase; 'raised' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A demur is a protest or hesitation voiced against something, an objection.

clue.text: Very little money for food

definitions.meaning: 'not a ...' means no money at all, so a ... is the smallest sum

explanation.surface: Having almost no cash to spend on something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean is slang for a tiny amount of cash and also a pulse eaten as food.

clue.text: Verify a small particular

parts.note: certain means particular, as in 'a certain person'

explanation.surface: A command to check one little detail.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for sure, to make certain, so to confirm or verify.

clue.text: Roman general contracted disease

indicators.note: contracted here means held within, so the letters lie inside Roman general

explanation.surface: A Roman commander caught an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted disease' reads as catching an illness; 'contracted' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mange is a skin condition of animals caused by mites, a disease.

clue.text: Good-bye to All That author's initials

indicators.note: initials are the first letters of each of the words to All That author's

explanation.surface: The initials of the author of Good-Bye to All That.
explanation.walkthrough: Good-Bye to All That is Robert Graves's memoir; his initials would be RG, but the letters come from the title words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British farewell, a casual way to say goodbye.

clue.text: Irene's wasted, having injected lousy chemical substance

indicators.note: having injected means taking something inside, so the shuffled name holds the other piece
wasted means wrecked, so the letters of Irene's are rearranged

parts.note: poxy is British slang for lousy, rubbish

explanation.surface: Irene is ruined after taking some dodgy drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irene's wasted' reads as Irene being drunk; 'wasted' gives ERESIN, and 'having injected' puts the slang word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Epoxy resin is a synthetic polymer used in strong glues and coatings, a chemical substance.
